governance.note: neiso-48 = the neiso-47 fast-start keeper recipe on current main (measured Algonquin/EIA-MA-citygate DAILY gas-hub basis overlay + dual-fuel oil re-attribution + EIA-930-pinned hydro budget with 2024 plant-capacity backfill + biomass/OTHER measured must-run + historic CAMPD outage overlay + dual-limb temperature-correlated reliability floor + floor-class outage exemption + post-solve ORDC scarcity-price overlay + tranche_startup_amortization + CC_REGULAR econ band 1.00->1.15) with ONE structural change: the CT_PEAKER temperature (tmax) reliability-floor limbs (Boston + Connecticut) are SCRUBBED (enabled True->False in data/raw/reference/reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv). Root cause (rule #17/#18, mirrors the CAISO caiso-52 CT scrub): the CT_PEAKER floor was an all-24h day-gated limb (no sub-daily window), so on any design-cooling day (tmax > ~30.7 C) it forced fast-start peakers at min-stable across ALL 24 hours. Measured effect on the neiso-47 recipe (current-main baseline A/B, this bundle vs neiso_ctbase): D4 off-window binding 0.72-0.76 (72-76% of floored energy fell OUTSIDE the h15-21 peak the floor's own hot-afternoon driver names) -> floor removed; C8 forced-energy share 0.47/0.78/0.47 (2023/24/25, gate <0.10) -> 0.00 in all years; C7 CT_PEAKER off-peak CV ratio 0.65/0.63/0.59 -> 0.76/0.86/0.79 (spikier, closer to the real peaker signature). Fast-start CTs (min-down <= 2h, startup < $30/MW) are economically dispatched for the peak, never day-ahead committed at a floor (rule #18); the removed forcing is not replaced by any new mechanism (zero-parameter deletion). Disclosed cost (rule #1, NOT to be won back with a floor): CT_PEAKER grid-delivered volume falls 0.079/0.144/0.184 -> 0.010/0.021/0.099 TWh; the ~0.07-0.12 TWh/yr is absorbed by the marginal CC_REGULAR (+0.07/+0.12/+0.09 TWh) at essentially the same price (dw-LMP +$0.02/+0.04/+0.06). Every other dispatch class moves < 0.0012 TWh; total generation, oil, coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables, CHP and CO2 are unchanged. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a residual; the LP is not pinned to actuals.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible from the committed bundle: scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso NEISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --commitment --reliability-floor --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly --gas-hub-basis-daily --scarcity-price-overlay --tranche-startup-amortization --out-dir results/calibration/neiso_ctscrub, with the two CT_PEAKER tmax limbs disabled in reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv (recorded in run_config.git.dirty + model_changes.diff). Leave-one-year-out (rule #22): the change is a zero-free-parameter mechanism DELETION (no value fitted to any year), so LOO degenerates to 'passes CT_PEAKER C7 & C8 in every year' — confirmed 2023/24/25 (C8 0.00 all years; C7 0.76/0.86/0.79). Ablation/A-B twin registered alongside: neiso_ctbase (identical recipe, CT floor ON) shows the pre-scrub failing state (C8 0.47/0.78/0.47 FAIL, D4 0.72-0.76 FAIL). REMAINING OPEN C7 GATE (out of scope of the CT-floor fix, unchanged by the scrub, pre-existing in neiso-47): ST_GAS diurnal shape still FAILS D1 (cv_ratio 35.4/0.0/0.0, profile_r 0.62/0.66/0.71) — a distinct steam-gas mechanism, ledgered below as the next NEISO root cause. NEISO overall determination therefore remains NOT-YET; this keeper is promoted as the most structurally faithful NEISO run (rule #1/#12), one confirmed flat-floor bug removed.

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage — per-class actuals are incomplete (audit 2026-07-04: 13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting; gas family incomplete). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which INCLUDES geothermal+biomass (~5.2 TWh); the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue documented for the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. When the full 2025 vintage reconciles, the per-class gate replaces this family fallback. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The post-solve ORDC scarcity overlay (ISO-NE-grounded LOLP curve: VOLL $2000 = Tariff III.1.10.1A offer cap, MCL 1200 MW ~ Millstone 3, sigma 900 MW = PAF Study 2022) fires and modifies econ_prices for capacity economics but does not change the persisted LP prices. The fast-start tranche pricing added in this run lifts the summer-evening and shoulder peak pricing but cannot produce >$300 cold-snap hours — that scarcity rent is the finite winter fuel INVENTORY the LP prices as an unlimited flow. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (docs/multi-iso/neiso-winter-fuel-inventory-plan-2026-07.md), NEVER via an offer adder tuned to the tail.

exceptions.magnitude: model 1.05 vs actual 2.08 TWh (-49.3%; was -64.6% on the neiso-44 base control)
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / winter-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. The fast-start tranche pricing + econ-band re-anchor recovered a third of the gap ENDOGENOUSLY (0.74 -> 1.05 TWh, no storage-formulation change — per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis, the PS number may only move downstream of price structure). The residual under-cycle is winter-concentrated: the LP's cold-month spread stays compressed at the dual-fuel oil-parity cap, and the real Northfield fleet additionally cycles near-daily for reserves/regulation the energy-only LP does not remunerate. Closes with the winter fuel-inventory build and/or in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage; never via a storage knob.

exceptions.classification: OPEN ROOT CAUSE (honest cost of killing ERCOT offer-band leakage, commit 0c6c833 / rule #25 — NOT this run's CT scrub)
exceptions.reason: neiso-47's price pass (-4.6/-2.3%) was partly produced by ERCOT-fitted CT_PEAKER/CC_CHP/ST_GAS econ bands that leaked cross-ISO into _NEISO_OFFER_CURVE; commit 0c6c833 killed that leakage (rule #25), de-leaking those bands to neutral 1.0. Model clearing prices fell ~$2/MWh as a result. This CT-floor scrub is price-neutral (A/B dw-LMP +$0.04). Closable ONLY by grounding real NEISO-measured CT/CC_CHP/ST_GAS part-load HR spreads (rule #1 second-step calibration), never by re-introducing the ERCOT-leaked bands (rule #25).

exceptions.metric: C7 / D1 ST_GAS off-peak diurnal shape (gated class)
exceptions.magnitude: profile_r 0.619 (<0.8); off-peak CV ratio 35.4 (model far too volatile)
exceptions.classification: OPEN ROOT CAUSE (distinct steam-gas mechanism; unchanged by the CT-floor scrub; pre-existing in neiso-47)
exceptions.reason: The remaining NEISO C7 gate after the CT_PEAKER fix. NEISO ST_GAS is a thin steam fleet whose P1/P2 profile alternates hyper-spiky (2023) and flat (2024/25) with profile_r < 0.8 — a steam-gas commitment/offer-shape question, separate from the CT reliability floor scrubbed here, and the recommended next NEISO item. Fix structurally, never re-tune to win C7 back (rules #1/#17-20). CT_PEAKER C7 now PASSES (cv_ratio 0.76/0.86/0.79).
